look_here_first: First check the plant base and leaf tips. Drummond's skullcap is a small taprooted annual with visibly glandular-hairy stems/calyces; its leaves are acute-tipped, and lower stem leaves may be shallowly crenate. Then confirm the small blue-violet corolla and the visorlike Scutellaria calyx appendage.

lookalikes.differences: Scutellaria wrightii: S. wrightii is a bushy perennial with several-many stems from a persistent base, rounded/obtuse entire leaves, minute pubescence and a smoother-looking calyx; its corolla is larger (mostly 13–18 mm) and its pedicel longer (3–3.5 mm). S. drummondii is annual, acute-leaved, visibly glandular-hairy and smaller-flowered. Scutellaria ovata: S. ovata is a much taller rhizomatous perennial (about 35–70 cm in the Williamson treatment) with much larger triangular-ovate, crenate leaves and much larger corollas (about 21–25 mm).
